calls.head: Like for like: Meyers vs. Klapka
calls.body: At home, the Kraken keep sending Meyers’s line (Winterton, Meyers and Douglas) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Lane Lambert keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.

calls.head: The Kraken don’t own Wolf
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Wolf has been shaky against the Kraken, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle a 63% chance, and they delivered.

CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 37% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Beniers wins it in overtime
paras: Yegor Sharangovich opened the scoring for the Flames midway through the first. Seattle had a goal taken off for offside later in the period, though it didn’t end up costing them. Berkly Catton tied it 1-1 for Seattle midway through the second. Matty Beniers won it 55 seconds into overtime.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Flames hit four posts and still lost. Joey Daccord made 25 saves for the Kraken, and Dustin Wolf stopped 27 of 29 at the other end.
Martin Pospíšil took three penalties on his own. The Kraken improved to 9-5-1, third in the Pacific, while the Flames fell to 7-8-1 but climbed to fifth in the Pacific.

items.text: Berkly Catton has a point in seven straight games.
Chandler Stephenson’s seven-game point streak against Calgary ended.
Matthew Wood made his Kraken debut, after three seasons with the Predators.
The Kraken lead the season series 3-1.
